title: He Took Six Wickets in Forty-Degree Heat. Two Days Later, Afghanistan Added Him to the ODI Squad.
excerpt: Mohammad Saleem's promotion from reserve to the playing squad for the India series is the fastest reward in Afghan cricket's recent history.
body:
Afghanistan's young fast bowler Mohammad Saleem has been added to the ODI squad for the three-match series against India, the Afghanistan Cricket Board announced on Wednesday. The promotion comes on the back of a performance in the one-off Test that earned the 23-year-old admiration from both camps.

Saleem was originally named among the reserves for the ODI assignment. His six-wicket haul in India's first innings at New Chandigarh, where temperatures crossed 40°C and the surface offered almost nothing for pace bowlers, changed the calculation. He finished with figures of 6 for 140 from 27 overs — the best by an Afghan fast bowler against India in Tests.

"He was just fantastic," Afghanistan head coach Richard Pybus told ESPNcricinfo. "If you come here and you take six wickets in extreme heat against high-quality batting, that goes very well, not just for him as a bowler, but for us as a side."

What He Did in Forty-Degree Heat

The conditions at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium were gruelling. India declared at 564 for 8, with Shubman Gill scoring 126 and Rishabh Pant adding 81. While Saleem's figures might look expensive at first glance, context changes the reading entirely. He bowled 27 overs on a surface that offered negligible seam movement, consistently touching 140 kph across long, disciplined spells.

He was not given the second new ball despite being the standout seamer. When asked about that decision, Pybus was candid: "I don't have any history with these guys before. So in terms of their combinations, this is part of my learning curve."

The ODI Series Ahead

The three-match series — Afghanistan's first-ever bilateral ODI assignment in India — begins on June 13 at the HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala. The second ODI moves to Lucknow on June 17, with the finale in Chennai on June 20.

Saleem joins a squad that already includes the firepower of Rashid Khan, the batting of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran, and the all-round experience of Mohammad Nabi and Azmatullah Omarzai. Both Rashid and Nabi missed the final training session in Mohali — Rashid is expected to join the squad directly in Dharamsala, while Nabi was sidelined by illness.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora following Afghan cricket's rise, Saleem represents a new archetype. Afghanistan has been synonymous with spin — Rashid Khan, Nangialai Kharoti, AM Ghazanfar. A fast bowler who can consistently trouble top-order batters in Indian conditions opens a different dimension for the team.

The updated Afghanistan ODI squad reads: Hashmatullah Shahidi (c), Rahmanullah Gurbaz (wk), Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Rahmat Shah, Ikram Alikhil (wk), Mohammad Nabi, Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan, Nangyal Kharotai, AM Ghazanfar, Zia Ur Rahman Sharifi, Fareed Malik, Bilal Sami, and Mohammad Saleem.

India, meanwhile, will be without Virat Kohli and Hardik Pandya for the series. Shubman Gill captains a squad that includes Rohit Sharma, Yashasvi Jaiswal, and uncapped prospects like Prince Yadav and Gurnoor Brar. The series marks the beginning of India's formal preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.

For an Afghan player who was a reserve 48 hours ago, the trajectory has been swift. On a surface that gave him nothing, Mohammad Saleem gave everything. Now he gets three more chances to prove it wasn't a one-off.
